""" import hashlib import json import os import subprocess import sys import time from pathlib import Path from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import ( Encoding, PublicFormat, PrivateFormat, NoEncryption ) from pyuheprng import UHEPRNG # github.com/ness-network/pyuheprng # ── Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── KEY_DIR = Path(os.getenv("KEY_DIR", "/mnt/ness/keys")) STORAGE_ROOT = Path(os.getenv("STORAGE_ROOT", "/mnt/ness")) NVS_NAMESPACE = "aix" NODE_NAME = os.getenv("NODE_NAME", "") # e.g. "mynode.ness" — set in /etc/ness/node.conf ENV_FILE = Path("/etc/ness/node.env") # written for systemd EnvironmentFile= ENTROPY_DRAWS = 6 # × 1024 bytes from os.urandom = 6144 bytes input UHEPRNG_BITS = 1536 # total bits mixed (paper §5.4 reference value) def main(): print("=== NESS first-boot provisioning ===") KEY_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (STORAGE_ROOT / "transcripts").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (STORAGE_ROOT / "blobs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if (KEY_DIR / "ed25519_pk.txt").exists(): print("[skip] Keys already provisioned.") _write_env() return # 1. Collect entropy print("[1/5] Collecting entropy...") entropy_pool = _collect_entropy() # 2. Seed pyuheprng and derive Ed25519 keypair (identity root) print("[2/5] Deriving Ed25519 identity key (Identity Bedrock)...") ed_sk, ed_pk_b64 = _derive_ed25519(entropy_pool) # 3. Derive Skywire keypair (secp256k1 transport address) print("[3/5] Deriving Skywire transport keypair...") sky_sk_hex, sky_pk_hex = _derive_skywire(entropy_pool, ed_sk) # 4. Write keys to F2FS (fscrypt-protected partition) print("[4/5] Writing keys to encrypted F2FS partition...") _write_keys(ed_sk, ed_pk_b64, sky_sk_hex, sky_pk_hex) _write_env(sky_pk_hex) # 5. Register identity in EmerNVS (WORM format, Identity Bedrock §5.1) print("[5/5] Registering identity in EmerNVS...") if NODE_NAME: _register_nvs(NODE_NAME, ed_pk_b64, sky_pk_hex) else: print(" [warn] NODE_NAME not set — skipping EmerNVS registration.") print(" Run: emercoin-cli name_new aix:<name> <worm_json> 365") print(" Or set NODE_NAME in /etc/ness/node.conf and re-run.") print("\n=== Provisioning complete ===") print(f" Ed25519 pubkey : {ed_pk_b64}") print(f" Skywire pubkey : {sky_pk_hex}") print(f" Keys at : {KEY_DIR}") print(f" Systemd env : {ENV_FILE}") # ── Entropy collection ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── def _collect_entropy() -> bytes: """ Mix: 1. Multiple os.urandom draws (kernel CSPRNG, ~256-bit security ceiling) 2. RC4OK from emercoin-cli (hardware-seeded RNG from EMC core) 3. Natural sources: CPU timing jitter, hardware identifiers, monotonic time Total input >> 256 bits for robustness against partial bias/leakage (§5.4). Security of resulting keys still rests on Ed25519 ~128-bit classical floor. """ pool = b"" # os.urandom — multiple draws for i in range(ENTROPY_DRAWS): chunk = os.urandom(1024) pool += chunk print(f" os.urandom draw {i+1}/{ENTROPY_DRAWS}: {len(chunk)} bytes") # RC4OK from emercoin-cli rc4ok = _emercoin_rc4ok() if rc4ok: pool += rc4ok print(f" RC4OK (emercoin-cli): {len(rc4ok)} bytes") else: print(" [warn] RC4OK unavailable — continuing without emercoin entropy") # Natural sources: CPU timing jitter jitter = _timing_jitter(samples=512) pool += jitter print(f" CPU timing jitter: {len(jitter)} bytes") # Hardware identifiers (serial, MAC) hw_bytes = _hardware_entropy() pool += hw_bytes print(f" Hardware identifiers: {len(hw_bytes)} bytes") # Monotonic nanosecond timestamp pool += str(time.time_ns()).encode() total_bits = len(pool) * 8 print(f" Total entropy pool: {len(pool)} bytes ({total_bits} bits input)") return pool def _emercoin_rc4ok() -> bytes: """ Request random bytes from emercoin-cli using RC4OK. emercoin-cli has a built-in RNG seeded from hardware/OS at startup. Returns raw bytes or empty if unavailable. """ try: result = subprocess.run( ["emercoin-cli", "makekeypair"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10 ) # makekeypair output includes fresh random material we can extract if result.returncode == 0: raw = result.stdout.strip().encode() # Hash it — we want entropy, not the actual key material return hashlib.sha512(raw).digest() * 4 # 256 bytes except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired): pass return b"" def _timing_jitter(samples: int = 512) -> bytes: """ Collect CPU timing jitter by measuring nanosecond-resolution loop timing. Captures low-order bits of time.time_ns() which vary with cache/pipeline state. """ jitter_bytes = [] for _ in range(samples): t0 = time.time_ns() # Tiny CPU-bound work to amplify jitter _ = hashlib.md5(os.urandom(4)).digest() t1 = time.time_ns() delta = (t1 - t0) & 0xFF # low byte jitter_bytes.append(delta) return bytes(jitter_bytes) def _hardware_entropy() -> bytes: """ Read hardware identifiers: eMMC CID, MAC address, CPU serial. Not secret — used only as additional mixing material. """ sources = [ "/sys/class/block/mmcblk0/device/cid", "/sys/class/net/eth0/address", "/sys/class/net/wlan0/address", "/proc/cpuinfo", "/etc/machine-id", ] data = b"" for src in sources: try: data += Path(src).read_bytes()[:64] except (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError): pass return data # ── Key derivation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── def _derive_ed25519(entropy_pool: bytes): """ Seed pyuheprng with entropy pool, extract 32-byte seed, derive Ed25519 keypair. Identity root per Identity Bedrock (Rompel OWF floor). """ prng = UHEPRNG() # Feed pool in 1024-byte blocks as the paper describes for i in range(0, len(entropy_pool), 1024): block = entropy_pool[i:i+1024] prng.hashPool(block) # Extract 32-byte (256-bit) seed seed = prng.bytes(32) sk = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(seed) pk = sk.public_key() pk_b = pk.public_bytes(Encoding.Raw, PublicFormat.Raw) pk_b64 = pk_b.hex() # hex for NVS/WORM compatibility return sk, pk_b64 def _derive_skywire(entropy_pool: bytes, ed_sk: Ed25519PrivateKey): """ Derive a secp256k1 keypair for Skywire transport. Deterministically derived from Ed25519 sk + entropy pool so the Skywire address is permanently tied to this box's identity. In production: feed this seed to skywire-cli keygen --seed <hex> or use privatenesstools keygen. """ # Sign a domain-separation string with Ed25519 sk — output is deterministic # and tied to the identity key, no fresh randomness needed here domain = b"ness:skywire:keygen:v1" sig = ed_sk.sign(domain) # Mix sig + entropy pool tail → 32-byte seed for secp256k1 sky_seed = hashlib.sha256(sig + entropy_pool[-512:]).digest() sky_seed_hex = sky_seed.hex() # Derive via skywire-cli if available, else return seed for manual use try: result = subprocess.run( ["skywire-cli", "config", "gen", "--is-hypervisor=false", "--seed", sky_seed_hex, "--dry-run"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15 ) if result.returncode == 0: cfg = json.loads(result.stdout) sk_hex = cfg.get("sk", sky_seed_hex) pk_hex = cfg.get("pk", "") return sk_hex, pk_hex except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired): pass # Fallback: return seed — operator feeds to skywire-cli manually print(" [warn] skywire-cli not available — Skywire seed written for manual keygen") return sky_seed_hex, "" # ── Key storage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── def _write_keys(ed_sk, ed_pk_b64: str, sky_sk_hex: str, sky_pk_hex: str): """ Write keys to F2FS fscrypt-protected partition. Ed25519 sk stored as raw hex — partition encryption is the protection layer. """ sk_bytes = ed_sk.private_bytes(Encoding.Raw, PrivateFormat.Raw, NoEncryption()) (KEY_DIR / "ed25519_sk.hex").write_text(sk_bytes.hex()) (KEY_DIR / "ed25519_pk.txt").write_text(ed_pk_b64) (KEY_DIR / "skywire_sk.hex").write_text(sky_sk_hex) (KEY_DIR / "skywire_pk.txt").write_text(sky_pk_hex) # Set restrictive permissions — fscrypt is primary but defence in depth for f in KEY_DIR.iterdir(): f.chmod(0o600) KEY_DIR.chmod(0o700) print(f" Keys written to {KEY_DIR} (fscrypt partition)") def _write_env(sky_pk_hex: str = ""): """ Write systemd EnvironmentFile so all NESS services share the pubkey. """ ENV_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) pk = sky_pk_hex or (KEY_DIR / "skywire_pk.txt").read_text().strip() \ if (KEY_DIR / "skywire_pk.txt").exists() else "" ed_pk = (KEY_DIR / "ed25519_pk.txt").read_text().strip() \ if (KEY_DIR / "ed25519_pk.txt").exists() else "" ENV_FILE.write_text( f"NODE_PUBKEY={pk}\n" f"NODE_ED25519_PK={ed_pk}\n" f"KEY_DIR={KEY_DIR}\n" f"STORAGE_ROOT={STORAGE_ROOT}\n" ) ENV_FILE.chmod(0o640) print(f" Systemd env written to {ENV_FILE}") # ── EmerNVS registration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── def _register_nvs(name: str, ed_pk_b64: str, sky_pk_hex: str): """ Publish Identity Bedrock WORM record to EmerNVS (§5.1). Ed25519 pubkey is identity root; Skywire pubkey is transport address. Record controlled by the EMC wallet key — separate concern from identity auth. """ worm = json.dumps({ "id": f"{NVS_NAMESPACE}:{name}", "pk": ed_pk_b64, # Ed25519 — identity root (Rompel floor) "skywire_pk": sky_pk_hex, # secp256k1 — transport "created": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()), "network": "ness", "version": "1", }) result = subprocess.run( ["emercoin-cli", "name_new", f"{NVS_NAMESPACE}:{name}", worm, "365"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30 ) if result.returncode != 0: print(f" [warn] EmerNVS registration failed: {result.stderr}") print(f" Manual registration command:") print(f" emercoin-cli name_new {NVS_NAMESPACE}:{name} '{worm}' 365") else: txid = result.stdout.strip() print(f" EmerNVS record published. txid: {txid}") (KEY_DIR / "nvs_txid.txt").write_text(txid) if __name__ == "__main__": if os.geteuid() != 0: print("Error: provisioning must run as root (fscrypt partition access)") sys.exit(1) main()
